newsitem.title: UK: Export surplus threatens world sugar prices - Man.
newsitem.headline: Export surplus threatens world sugar prices - Man.

text.p: World sugar prices could come under pressure later in 1996/97 with the possibility of raw sugar exports from India and the release of white sugar surpluses from Eastern Europe, E D & F Man said on Thursday.

In its first estimate of the 1996/97 sugar balance, Man said trade support of world prices would be increasingly tested by the emergence of surplus stocks in India and three eastern European nations -- Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
"The overriding picture that is emerging in these four countries is that an export buffer is building up that could unleash a sizeable tonnage of sugar onto the world market," the Man report said.

It added that the determining factor in India rested with the pace of deregulation of the domestic sugar economy and said mills could cut their milling process short to produce raws rather than the usual plantation whites.

"It is expected that in search of additional export markets, India will export some 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes of raw sugar," it said. India was also sitting on sugar stocks amounting to 60 percent of the country's annual consumption.

"The possibility of raw sugar exports becomes more effective as white premium values fall and the extra value of whites moves closer to the marginal cost savings of producing raws instead of whites," the Man report added.

Many Indian millers remained convinced that they were better off retaining their surplus sugar in order to have adequate supplies when the anticipated fall in national production occurred in two years' time, it said.
But in Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic the deciding factor would be the prospect of falling local prices.

In Poland, the domestic output and the subsidised quotas totalled 1.743 million tonnes, implying that once domestic consumption was taken into account, some 243,000 tonnes could potentially be exported or moved abroad at protected prices.
This would leave over 200,000 tonnes of Polish sugar to be dumped on the world market unless a large tonnage was taken into intervention, Man said.

"Hungary and the Czech Republic too are expected to show a surplus of over 80,000 and 90,000 tonnes respectively -- some of this surplus is likely to be exported across the border to neighbouring countries," it added.

Although the potential Polish, Hungarian and Czech exports helped to substitute the expected decline in this year's Ukrainian exports, the trend towards higher white sugar import tariffs had reduced eastern Europe's forecast whites demand from nearly 4.3 million tonnes to under 3.5 million this season.
